title: A Conditional Reconstruction of the Quark Sector: CKM Mixing, Mass Ratios, and the QCD Coupling
content: The reconstruction programme explores a structural layer logically prior to dynamical evolution, where closure and persistence conditions constrain the identities and inputs subsequently represented by effective fields. We extend this approach to quark flavor and strong-response normalization, retaining the Standard Model and quantum chromodynamics as the effective descriptions of interactions and evolution. Quark degrees of freedom are interpreted as sectoral read-outs of a common hadronic closure structure. A shared electromagnetic capacity, transported finite interfaces, and explicit correspondence assumptions organize an exactly unitary Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix, light-quark mass ratios, and a five-flavor strong-coupling boundary value of approximately 0.118243 in the modified minimal subtraction scheme at the Z-boson mass. The finite construction establishes resolved and orientation-forgetting channel counts, consistent probability read-outs, and a protected response subspace. Eliminating the common capacity yields cross-sector constraints, including a linear relation between two light-quark mass ratios. These relations provide targets for prospective tests with compatible conventions and correlations. Agreement with historical data is treated as retrodiction because observed patterns informed parts of the discrete assignments. The interpretation, mathematical consequences, and remaining physical assumptions are distinguished throughout. Independent selection of phase and mass rules, and justification of renormalization matching, remain necessary for a complete structural derivation.
